Coral reefs cover less than one percent of the ocean floor. But they support about a quarter of all marine species. Rising sea temperatures cause coral bleaching. This is a process where corals expel the algae living in their tissues and turn white. If high temperatures continue, the corals can die. This threatens the ecosystems and coastal communities that depend on them.

Coral reefs cover less than one percent of the ocean floor, yet they support approximately a quarter of all marine species. Rising sea temperatures induce coral bleaching, a phenomenon whereby corals expel the symbiotic algae residing within their tissues, resulting in a white discoloration. Consequently, prolonged exposure to elevated temperatures can lead to coral mortality, thereby posing a significant threat to both the dependent marine ecosystems and coastal communities.
